sometimes drifting for miles always standing straight but here is the strange part most fallen logs slowly soak up water and sink this one has stayed afloat through more than a hundred winters stones probably trapped in its roots keep the bottom heavy why it never sinks is still debated the icy clean water may slow its decay some rangers say storms roll in whenever the old man is tied down it is only folklore our next lake has a stranger habit it disappears high in the oregon cascades lost lake looks ordinary in spring snowmelt fills it pine trees ring the water ducks rest on its calm surface but as summer arrives the water starts to drop not the way a puddle dries in the sun it drains away as if someone pulled a plug the secret is in the lakebed holes leading into old lava tubes as the level falls water swirls quietly into them like a bathtub draining into stone by late summer the lake is often a dry meadow full of wildflowers then rain and snow return and it fills again year after year here is the turn the lake is not really disappearing the lava rock beneath it is full of cracks and tubes and it works like a giant sponge scientists think the water seeps through the mountains and joins hidden underground reservoirs the same kind that feed icy springs and rivers lower down so the lake is a doorway not an ending our next mystery also hides underground but what comes out of it is not water it is fire in a quiet park in western new york a creek spills over layered gray rock it is a small waterfall the kind you could easily walk past until you look behind the falling water tucked in a small hollow in the rock a flame is burning it stays lit while water pours past it it is not magic natural gas leaks through cracks in the rock and once lit it can burn for long stretches through rain snow and spray when it does go out visitors usually relight it in winter the flame can glow behind a curtain of ice like a lantern hidden in the falls gas seeps are common here but when scientists measured this one it held unusually high amounts of ethane and propane gases usually made in very hot rock but the rock beneath these falls was likely never hot enough to cook gas like that by the usual rules this flame should not exist researchers suggested the gas may form another way through a slower process in cooler rock or travel from far below the idea is still being tested fire hidden in water is strange but our last mystery is stranger it is a river that seems to fall into the earth and never come back in the woods of northern minnesota near lake superior the brool river
